n0.hypothesis: Maximize held-out macro detection recall for silent agentic-RL contract failures while keeping clean-fixture false-positive rate at or below 5 percent
n0.insight:
[from n1] Successful agentic-RL execution does not establish typed reward-boundary equivalence; production-boundary positive controls are required
[from n2] Reward contracts must cover namespace flow and structured failure provenance in addition to schema types
[from n3] Preflight identifiability needs declared treatment aliases and nondegenerate group variance
[from n5] Frozen reward-contract checks transfer to natural missing-reward defaults in unseen systems; boundary relevance must be reported separately from detection correctness

n1.hypothesis: Typed serialization contracts catch silent reward corruption that exit-code and finite-metric checks miss
n1.insight: Typed equivalence must be checked at the exact reward boundary, not inferred from successful parsing or process exit

n2.hypothesis: Semantic trajectory and reward invariants are required because schema-valid traces can still be scientifically invalid
n2.insight:
Schema validity is insufficient when producer and consumer namespaces differ or failure status is erased

n3.insight: Identical treatments are acceptable only when preregistered as equivalence controls; grouped estimators need an explicit variance precondition

n4.hypothesis: The same silent typed-boundary failure appears naturally in at least one independent development framework
n4.insight: Cross-system recurrence occurred at the broader reward-contract layer, not the exact serialization subtype

n5.insight: External transfer is supported at evaluator-coercion and eval-replay boundaries, but the slime case is not evidence of core training-path prevalence
